AWPTCM-T33246.objective:
• When an IP address is removed from a device, its ARP entry remains in the SNMP ARP polling table on the monitoring device for the full configured polling interval.
  • After the ARP polling interval expires, the monitoring device updates the ARP entry to reflect the new owner of the IP address.
  • The configured snmp-discovery arp-polling-interval value controls the time before the monitoring device updates a stale ARP polling entry.
  • show arp global accurately displays the current owner and polling state of entries managed by SNMP ARP polling.
  • When a new device claims an IP address previously held by another device, the monitoring device updates the ARP polling entry to the new owner after the polling interval.
  • Setting the polling interval to 0 (or disabling the feature) prevents automatic ARP entry updates via polling.

steps.description: Note: Thin historical coverage. Objectives derived from case precondition and steps. Related cases linked in Traceability.
Configure snmp-discovery arp-polling-interval on the monitoring device. Verify the initial ARP entry for the target IP shows the correct owner in show arp global.
Remove the IP address from the original owner. Verify the ARP entry persists with the original MAC for the full polling interval.
After the polling interval expires, assign the same IP to a new device. Verify the monitoring device updates the ARP entry to the new MAC.
Test with different polling interval values and confirm the update timing matches the configured value.
Verify show arp global accurately reflects the current owner and polling state throughout the test.
Set the polling interval to 0 (or disable the feature) and confirm no automatic ARP entry updates occur via polling.
